title: Supported endpoint equation of a normalized comparison
statement: For l,Y,E,pi,n,A,hA and q as in UniformizerSquareData [def-diagonal-uniformizer-root-frame], let s:quotientRight(q) ~= restriction(q) followed by cyclicRight(q) be GIVEN with RestrictionNormalized(q,s) [def-diagonal-coefficient-route-comparison]. Then SourceEquation(q,s) [def-diagonal-coefficient-route-equations] holds. This asserts only the supported derived endpoint equation, not existence or uniqueness of s.

source.place: paragraph (1), finite cyclic reduction followed by finite coefficient extension

proof.text: Transpose under the cyclic adjunction. The restrictionMate definition gives the quotient endpoint transpose followed by the right-functor comparison. Transpose the finite realization and the scalar endpoints using Endpoint.normalization and composition of exact single comparisons.

Forget the resulting ordinary equation. RestrictionNormalized cancels the inverse-realization counits. FiniteSourceComparison.normalization and FiniteRealization.unit_normalization reduce both sides to unital maps from pulled-back Z_l to constant A. Reduction modulo l^(n+1) and generation by one give their equality. The source_normalization of maps.source identifies its constant-generator map with the same coefficient map. Sheafification, direct image, and reversal of the adjunction transpositions give SourceEquation.

theorem diagonalCyclic_uniformizerSource_equation
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E) (n : ℕ)
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    (hA : ((l ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : A) = 0)
    (q : UniformizerSquareData l Y E π n A hA)
    (s : q.quotientRight ≅ q.restriction ⋙ q.cyclicRight)
    (hs : q.RestrictionNormalized s) :
    sourceEquation% (UniformizerSquareData.endpointSquare l Y E π n A hA q) s
